_README:
Golden set for the LLM claim pre-fill (P1). Each example holds the extractor inputs (abstract, statement, topics) and the hand-curated 'gold' review fields a human would accept. '_recorded' is the model suggestion last captured for the SAME prompt: `scripts/eval_claim_prefill.py --record-live` (AI_PROVIDER=anthropic) overwrites it from a real call AND reports live accuracy vs gold; `scripts/eval_claim_prefill.py --write-fixtures` replays it into tests/fixtures/ai/ so CI runs offline and deterministically (AI_PROVIDER=cache). The offline eval therefore measures a REGRESSION of the recorded outputs against gold, not a fresh live call -- '_recorded' deliberately diverges from 'gold' on the harder cases so the numbers stay honest. evidence_strength uses the claim schema's vocabulary low|moderate|strong (schemas/claim.schema.json), rendered into the prompt from common.EVIDENCE_STRENGTH_VALUES; null means the abstract does not support that field. DO NOT wire these into data/ -- they are an evaluation artifact only. NOTE (v7): the 'high' -> 'strong' switch was a VOCABULARY migration of the existing recordings, not a fresh live measurement -- the same judgement under the name the data model accepts. v7 also newly permits evidence_strength=null when the abstract does not reveal the study type, and THAT change is untested until the next --record-live run. The offline regression stays valid as a drift check; live v7 accuracy is unmeasured.

SYNTHETIC EVALUATION DATA. Every abstract in this file was written for this evaluation. None is a real publication: there are no authors, no journal, no DOI and no URL, and none may be invented. Each example's gold_appraisal therefore carries source_provenance 'synthetic_eval_case' and source_verified 'false'. Their job is to exercise the classification logic, not to represent scientific evidence -- validate_data.py rejects a claim marked synthetic_eval_case in data/claims/ for exactly that reason.

TWO LABEL LAYERS, on purpose. 'gold' holds the LEGACY review fields (age_range, outcome, context, evidence_strength) and is FROZEN: it is the calibration reference for '_recorded', a live model response captured under prompt claim-prefill-v7, and the CI gates in .github/workflows/validate.yml are measured against it. Re-labelling it without re-recording would fail those gates for a reason that has nothing to do with the model.
'gold_appraisal' holds the SUCCESSOR model (scripts/appraisal.py): evidence_certainty plus the dimensions the old single value conflated. It is what a reviewer should apply today. Where the two disagree, the disagreement is data -- scripts/eval_agreement.py --legacy-drift reports it.

examples.abstract: We synthesise 18 classroom studies of AI literacy instruction in European primary schools. We find that structured AI literacy lessons improve pupils' ability to critically evaluate machine-generated outputs. Effects were consistent across the reviewed interventions.
examples.statement: We find that structured AI literacy lessons improve pupils' ability to critically evaluate machine-generated outputs.

gold.outcome: Pupils become better at critically evaluating machine-generated outputs.
gold.context: Systematic review of AI literacy lessons in European primary school classrooms.

_recorded.outcome: Structured AI literacy lessons improve pupils' ability to critically evaluate machine-generated outputs.
_recorded.context: A synthesis of 18 classroom studies of AI literacy instruction in European primary schools.

examples.abstract: A randomised controlled trial with 240 secondary students in Germany evaluated a block-based programming curriculum. Students in the treatment group showed significantly higher computational thinking scores than controls. The intervention ran for one semester.
examples.statement: Students in the treatment group showed significantly higher computational thinking scores than controls.

gold.outcome: Block-based programming raises computational thinking scores.
gold.context: One-semester randomised controlled trial in German secondary schools.

_recorded.outcome: Students receiving the block-based programming intervention achieved significantly higher computational thinking scores than the control group.
_recorded.context: A one-semester block-based programming curriculum delivered to secondary school students in Germany.

examples.abstract: This study examined project-based collaborative learning in middle-school science classrooms across three districts. Results indicate that sustained group projects improved students' collaboration and peer-feedback skills. Teachers reported higher engagement.
examples.statement: Results indicate that sustained group projects improved students' collaboration and peer-feedback skills.

gold.outcome: Group projects improve collaboration and peer-feedback skills.
gold.context: Multi-district study of project-based science learning in middle schools.

_recorded.outcome: Sustained group projects improved students' collaboration and peer-feedback skills.
_recorded.context: Middle-school science classrooms across three districts using project-based collaborative learning.

examples.abstract: We taught a data literacy module to 95 high-school students and measured changes in their ability to interpret charts and detect misleading statistics. Post-test scores improved, with the largest gains for students with low prior numeracy. The module lasted six weeks.
examples.statement: Post-test scores improved, with the largest gains for students with low prior numeracy.

gold.outcome: A data literacy module improves chart interpretation, especially for low-numeracy students.
gold.context: Six-week data literacy module with high-school students.

_recorded.outcome: Students' post-test scores on interpreting charts and detecting misleading statistics improved, with the largest gains among students with low prior numeracy.
_recorded.context: A six-week data literacy module delivered to 95 high-school students.

examples.abstract: A meta-analysis of 32 studies investigated self-regulated learning interventions for elementary pupils. The evidence suggests that explicit goal-setting and self-monitoring routines modestly improve task persistence. Heterogeneity across studies was high.
examples.statement: The evidence suggests that explicit goal-setting and self-monitoring routines modestly improve task persistence.

gold.outcome: Goal-setting and self-monitoring routines modestly improve task persistence.
gold.context: Meta-analysis of self-regulated learning interventions in elementary schools.

_recorded.outcome: Explicit goal-setting and self-monitoring routines modestly improve task persistence.
_recorded.context: Meta-analysis of 32 studies on self-regulated learning interventions for elementary school pupils.

examples.abstract: In a quasi-experimental design, two secondary cohorts followed a design-thinking unit. The treatment cohort produced more original and more feasible solutions on a standardised creativity rubric. Sample size was modest at 84 students.
examples.statement: The treatment cohort produced more original and more feasible solutions on a standardised creativity rubric.

gold.outcome: A design-thinking unit increases originality and feasibility of student solutions.
gold.context: Quasi-experimental design-thinking unit in secondary cohorts.

_recorded.outcome: The treatment cohort produced more original and more feasible solutions on a standardised creativity rubric.
_recorded.context: Quasi-experimental study with two secondary-school cohorts following a design-thinking unit.

examples.abstract: This policy report reviews national digital citizenship curricula. It argues that media-evaluation skills should be introduced earlier, but it presents no new measured learning outcomes. Recommendations target ministries of education.
examples.statement: It argues that media-evaluation skills should be introduced earlier, but it presents no new measured learning outcomes.

gold.context: Policy report reviewing national digital citizenship curricula.

_recorded.context: A policy report reviewing national digital citizenship curricula, with recommendations targeted at ministries of education.

examples.abstract: We compared interactive simulations to traditional lectures for teaching mechanics to 11th-grade physics students. Students using simulations demonstrated deeper conceptual understanding on a transfer test. The study involved four classes.
examples.statement: Students using simulations demonstrated deeper conceptual understanding on a transfer test.

gold.outcome: Interactive simulations deepen conceptual understanding of mechanics.
gold.context: Classroom comparison of simulations versus lectures in 11th-grade physics.

_recorded.outcome: Students using interactive simulations showed deeper conceptual understanding on a transfer test than those taught with traditional lectures.
_recorded.context: Physics instruction for 11th-grade students across four classes, comparing interactive simulations to traditional lectures in mechanics.

examples.abstract: A systematic review of reciprocal teaching examined its effect on reading comprehension in upper-primary classrooms. Results show consistent, moderate improvements in comprehension across 21 studies. The approach was robust to different text genres.
examples.statement: Results show consistent, moderate improvements in comprehension across 21 studies.

gold.outcome: Reciprocal teaching consistently and moderately improves reading comprehension.
gold.context: Systematic review of reciprocal teaching in upper-primary classrooms.

_recorded.outcome: Reciprocal teaching produced consistent, moderate improvements in reading comprehension.
_recorded.context: Systematic review of reciprocal teaching interventions in upper-primary classrooms across 21 studies.

examples.abstract: An adaptive AI tutoring system was deployed for algebra practice with 310 secondary students over eight weeks. Students using the tutor solved more problems correctly than a worksheet control group. Gains were largest among initially struggling students.
examples.statement: Students using the tutor solved more problems correctly than a worksheet control group.

gold.outcome: An adaptive AI tutor improves algebra problem-solving accuracy.
gold.context: Eight-week deployment of an AI algebra tutor in secondary schools.

_recorded.outcome: Students using the AI tutor solved more algebra problems correctly than a worksheet control group, with the largest gains among initially struggling students.
_recorded.context: Secondary school algebra practice using an adaptive AI tutoring system deployed over eight weeks with 310 students.

examples.abstract: A classroom social-emotional learning program for early primary children was evaluated with teacher ratings. Children in the program showed improved emotional regulation and fewer conflicts. The study used a waitlist control.
examples.statement: Children in the program showed improved emotional regulation and fewer conflicts.

gold.outcome: A social-emotional learning program improves emotional regulation and reduces conflicts.
gold.context: Waitlist-controlled SEL program in early primary classrooms.

_recorded.outcome: Children in the program showed improved emotional regulation and fewer conflicts according to teacher ratings.
_recorded.context: Early primary classroom social-emotional learning program evaluated with teacher ratings using a waitlist control.

examples.abstract: This working paper describes an after-school robotics club and reports preliminary engagement data. We present a six-step design for the club's activities. No comparison group or learning outcome was measured.
examples.statement: We present a six-step design for the club's activities.

gold.context: Working paper describing an after-school robotics club design.

_recorded.context: An after-school robotics club described in a working paper, reporting preliminary engagement data with a six-step activity design.

examples.abstract: We studied automated writing feedback for argumentative essays among 150 high-school students. Students who received automated feedback revised more substantively and improved essay quality scores. Improvements held at a delayed post-test.
examples.statement: Students who received automated feedback revised more substantively and improved essay quality scores.

gold.outcome: Automated feedback leads to more substantive revision and higher essay quality.
gold.context: Study of automated essay feedback with high-school writers.

_recorded.outcome: Students receiving automated feedback revised more substantively and achieved higher essay quality scores, with improvements maintained at a delayed post-test.
_recorded.context: Study of automated writing feedback for argumentative essays among 150 high-school students.

examples.abstract: Guided-inquiry biology lessons were compared with direct instruction in lower-secondary classrooms. Students in the inquiry condition retained more conceptual knowledge after six months. Engagement measures also favoured inquiry.
examples.statement: Students in the inquiry condition retained more conceptual knowledge after six months.

gold.outcome: Guided inquiry improves long-term retention of biology concepts.
gold.context: Comparison of guided inquiry and direct instruction in lower-secondary biology.

_recorded.outcome: Students in the guided-inquiry condition retained more conceptual knowledge after six months than those in direct instruction.
_recorded.context: Lower-secondary biology classrooms comparing guided-inquiry lessons with direct instruction.

examples.abstract: A gamified vocabulary app was trialled with primary English-language learners. Children using the app learned and retained more vocabulary than those using flashcards. The trial ran for four weeks with 120 pupils.
examples.statement: Children using the app learned and retained more vocabulary than those using flashcards.

gold.outcome: A gamified app improves vocabulary learning and retention over flashcards.
gold.context: Four-week trial of a gamified vocabulary app with primary language learners.

_recorded.outcome: Children using the gamified app learned and retained more vocabulary than those using flashcards.
_recorded.context: A four-week trial with 120 primary-school English-language learners comparing a gamified vocabulary app with flashcards.

examples.abstract: This review synthesises peer-tutoring programs in secondary mathematics. Findings indicate small-to-moderate gains in achievement for both tutors and tutees. Effects were stronger in structured, well-monitored programs.
examples.statement: Findings indicate small-to-moderate gains in achievement for both tutors and tutees.

gold.outcome: Peer tutoring yields small-to-moderate achievement gains for tutors and tutees.
gold.context: Review of peer-tutoring programs in secondary mathematics.

_recorded.outcome: Peer tutoring produced small-to-moderate achievement gains for both tutors and tutees, with stronger effects in structured, well-monitored programs.
_recorded.context: Review of peer-tutoring programs in secondary mathematics education.

examples.abstract: We compared tablet-based and paper-based handwriting instruction for first graders. Both groups improved legibility, with no significant difference between conditions. The study followed 60 children over a term.
examples.statement: Both groups improved legibility, with no significant difference between conditions.

gold.outcome: Tablet and paper handwriting instruction improve legibility equally.
gold.context: Term-long comparison of tablet versus paper handwriting instruction for first graders.

_recorded.outcome: Both tablet-based and paper-based handwriting instruction improved legibility, with no significant difference between the two conditions.
_recorded.context: First-grade schoolchildren receiving handwriting instruction via either tablet-based or paper-based methods over one term.

examples.abstract: A flipped-classroom model was implemented in upper-secondary chemistry. Students completed more practice in class and achieved higher exam scores than in the prior traditional year. The comparison was non-randomised.
examples.statement: Students completed more practice in class and achieved higher exam scores than in the prior traditional year.

gold.outcome: A flipped classroom increases in-class practice and exam scores in chemistry.
gold.context: Non-randomised flipped-classroom implementation in upper-secondary chemistry.

_recorded.outcome: Students engaged in more in-class practice and achieved higher exam scores than in the previous traditional year.
_recorded.context: Upper-secondary chemistry classes using a flipped-classroom instructional model, compared non-randomly with a prior traditional year.

examples.abstract: A review of growth-mindset interventions across school ages reports that effects on achievement are small and concentrated among disadvantaged students. Many studies had methodological limitations. The authors urge cautious interpretation.
examples.statement: A review of growth-mindset interventions across school ages reports that effects on achievement are small and concentrated among disadvantaged students.

gold.outcome: Growth-mindset interventions yield small achievement effects, mainly for disadvantaged students.
gold.context: Review of growth-mindset interventions across school ages.

_recorded.outcome: Growth-mindset interventions have small effects on achievement, concentrated among disadvantaged students.
_recorded.context: A review of growth-mindset interventions conducted across school ages.

examples.abstract: An unplugged computing curriculum was evaluated with early-primary pupils who had no computer access. Pupils improved on algorithmic-thinking tasks compared with a control class. The intervention used physical games and cards.
examples.statement: Pupils improved on algorithmic-thinking tasks compared with a control class.

gold.outcome: An unplugged computing curriculum improves algorithmic thinking.
gold.context: Evaluation of an unplugged computing curriculum with early-primary pupils.

_recorded.outcome: Pupils showed improved performance on algorithmic-thinking tasks relative to a control class.
_recorded.context: An unplugged computing curriculum using physical games and cards was delivered to early-primary pupils without computer access.

examples.abstract: A virtual-reality history experience was tested with secondary students. Students reported high engagement, but knowledge-test gains did not differ from a video condition. The sample comprised two classes.
examples.statement: Students reported high engagement, but knowledge-test gains did not differ from a video condition.

gold.outcome: VR history boosts engagement but not knowledge gains over video.
gold.context: Classroom test of a VR history experience in secondary students.

_recorded.outcome: Students reported high engagement, but knowledge-test gains did not differ from a video condition.
_recorded.context: A virtual-reality history learning experience tested with secondary school students in two classes.

examples.abstract: This study analysed completion patterns in a university MOOC for adult professionals. Learners who set weekly goals completed more modules. The cohort ranged from 22 to 55 years old.
examples.statement: Learners who set weekly goals completed more modules.

gold.outcome: Weekly goal-setting raises MOOC module completion.
gold.context: Analysis of completion patterns in an adult-professional university MOOC.

_recorded.outcome: Learners who set weekly goals completed more modules than those who did not.
_recorded.context: A university MOOC for adult professionals aged 22 to 55, examining self-regulation through goal-setting in online learning.

examples.abstract: We evaluated a manipulatives-based number-sense program with 130 preschool children in two countries. Children in the program showed stronger early numeracy, particularly in counting and magnitude comparison. The program ran for ten weeks with trained educators.
examples.statement: Children in the program showed stronger early numeracy, particularly in counting and magnitude comparison.

gold.outcome: A manipulatives-based program strengthens preschoolers' early numeracy.
gold.context: Ten-week manipulatives number-sense program with preschool children in two countries.

_recorded.outcome: Children in the program showed stronger early numeracy, particularly in counting and magnitude comparison.
_recorded.context: A ten-week manipulatives-based number-sense intervention delivered by trained educators to preschool children across two countries.

examples.abstract: A systematic review of 28 trials examined systematic synthetic phonics in the first years of formal schooling. The evidence consistently shows improved word reading and decoding accuracy. Effects were robust across languages with transparent orthographies.
examples.statement: The evidence consistently shows improved word reading and decoding accuracy.

gold.outcome: Systematic synthetic phonics improves early word reading and decoding.
gold.context: Systematic review of synthetic phonics trials in the first years of schooling.

_recorded.outcome: Systematic synthetic phonics instruction is associated with improved word reading and decoding accuracy.
_recorded.context: Systematic review of 28 trials of systematic synthetic phonics instruction during the first years of formal schooling, across languages with transparent orthographies.

examples.abstract: A cyber-safety curriculum was delivered to middle-school students across eleven schools. Students who completed it reported fewer risky online disclosures and better password practices at a two-month follow-up. The design was a matched-school comparison.
examples.statement: Students who completed it reported fewer risky online disclosures and better password practices at a two-month follow-up.

gold.outcome: A cyber-safety curriculum reduces risky online disclosures and improves password practices.
gold.context: Matched-school comparison of a cyber-safety curriculum in middle schools.

_recorded.outcome: Students who completed the curriculum reported fewer risky online disclosures and better password practices at a two-month follow-up.
_recorded.context: A cyber-safety curriculum delivered to middle-school students across eleven schools.

examples.abstract: A budgeting simulation game was trialled with 180 secondary students to teach personal finance. Players improved their budgeting knowledge and reported greater confidence managing money. The study used a pre-post design without a control group.
examples.statement: Players improved their budgeting knowledge and reported greater confidence managing money.

gold.outcome: A budgeting game improves students' budgeting knowledge and money confidence.
gold.context: Pre-post trial of a budgeting simulation game with secondary students.

_recorded.outcome: Students improved their budgeting knowledge and reported greater confidence in managing money.
_recorded.context: Secondary school setting using a budgeting simulation game to teach personal finance.

examples.abstract: A small quasi-experiment gave 48 primary children weekly music training and measured executive-function tasks. The trained group showed modest gains in working memory and inhibitory control. The sample was small and not randomised.
examples.statement: The trained group showed modest gains in working memory and inhibitory control.

gold.outcome: Music training yields modest working-memory and inhibitory-control gains.
gold.context: Small non-randomised quasi-experiment of music training with primary children.

_recorded.outcome: Children who received music training showed modest gains in working memory and inhibitory control.
_recorded.context: A quasi-experimental study of primary school children receiving weekly music training.

examples.abstract: Structured classroom debate was introduced in upper-secondary civics lessons across six schools. Students improved measurably in argument quality and willingness to consider opposing views. Teachers implemented a common debate protocol.
examples.statement: Students improved measurably in argument quality and willingness to consider opposing views.

gold.outcome: Structured debate improves argument quality and openness to opposing views.
gold.context: Multi-school study of structured debate in upper-secondary civics.

_recorded.outcome: Students improved in argument quality and willingness to consider opposing views.
_recorded.context: Structured classroom debate intervention using a common protocol in upper-secondary civics lessons across six schools.

examples.abstract: A multisensory reading app for children with dyslexia was evaluated against standard remediation. App users improved decoding speed and accuracy more than the comparison group. The trial enrolled 72 children over twelve weeks.
examples.statement: App users improved decoding speed and accuracy more than the comparison group.

gold.outcome: A multisensory app improves decoding speed and accuracy for children with dyslexia.
gold.context: Twelve-week controlled trial of a multisensory dyslexia app versus standard remediation.

_recorded.outcome: Children using the app showed greater improvement in decoding speed and accuracy than those receiving standard remediation.
_recorded.context: A twelve-week trial with 72 children with dyslexia comparing a multisensory reading app to standard remediation.

examples.abstract: A tablet self-monitoring tool was tested with primary students showing attention difficulties. Using the tool, students reduced off-task behaviour and completed more independent work. The study used a single-case multiple-baseline design.
examples.statement: Using the tool, students reduced off-task behaviour and completed more independent work.

gold.outcome: A self-monitoring tool reduces off-task behaviour and increases independent work.
gold.context: Single-case multiple-baseline study of a self-monitoring tool with inattentive primary students.

_recorded.outcome: Students reduced off-task behaviour and increased completion of independent work when using the self-monitoring tool.
_recorded.context: Primary school students with attention difficulties used a tablet-based self-monitoring intervention.

examples.abstract: This systematic review synthesised studies of academic acceleration for high-ability students. Across the evidence, accelerated students achieved more without social-emotional harm. The review covered both grade-skipping and subject acceleration.
examples.statement: Across the evidence, accelerated students achieved more without social-emotional harm.

gold.outcome: Acceleration raises achievement for high-ability students without social-emotional harm.
gold.context: Systematic review of grade-skipping and subject acceleration for gifted students.

_recorded.outcome: Accelerated high-ability students achieved higher academic outcomes without negative social-emotional effects.
_recorded.context: Systematic review of academic acceleration (grade-skipping and subject acceleration) for high-ability students.

examples.abstract: A place-based outdoor science unit was compared with classroom-only instruction in two primary cohorts. Outdoor learners gained more environmental knowledge and reported more positive attitudes to science. The comparison was quasi-experimental.
examples.statement: Outdoor learners gained more environmental knowledge and reported more positive attitudes to science.

gold.outcome: Place-based outdoor science improves environmental knowledge and attitudes.
gold.context: Quasi-experimental comparison of outdoor versus classroom science in primary cohorts.

_recorded.outcome: Outdoor learners gained more environmental knowledge and reported more positive attitudes toward science compared with classroom-only learners.
_recorded.context: Primary-school science instruction comparing a place-based outdoor unit with classroom-only teaching across two cohorts.

examples.abstract: A review of spaced retrieval practice in schools analysed its effect on durable learning. Findings show that distributing retrieval over time reliably improves long-term retention compared with massed study. The benefit held across subjects and school ages.
examples.statement: Findings show that distributing retrieval over time reliably improves long-term retention compared with massed study.

gold.outcome: Spaced retrieval practice reliably improves long-term retention over massed study.
gold.context: Review of spaced retrieval practice across school subjects and ages.

_recorded.outcome: Distributing retrieval practice over time improves long-term retention compared with massed study.
_recorded.context: A review of spaced retrieval practice in school settings across various subjects and school ages.

examples.abstract: We studied translanguaging pedagogy in bilingual primary classrooms over a school year. Pupils allowed to draw on both languages understood science content better and participated more. The study used teacher logs and content assessments.
examples.statement: Pupils allowed to draw on both languages understood science content better and participated more.

gold.outcome: Translanguaging pedagogy improves bilingual pupils' content understanding and participation.
gold.context: Year-long study of translanguaging in bilingual primary science classrooms.

_recorded.outcome: Pupils allowed to use both languages showed better understanding of science content and increased participation.
_recorded.context: Year-long study in bilingual primary school classrooms using a translanguaging pedagogy intervention, assessed via teacher logs and content assessments.

examples.abstract: An AI tool giving real-time feedback on student code was deployed in lower-secondary computing. Students using it fixed bugs faster and submitted more working programs than a control class. The deployment lasted seven weeks.
examples.statement: Students using it fixed bugs faster and submitted more working programs than a control class.

gold.outcome: An AI code-feedback tool speeds debugging and increases working submissions.
gold.context: Seven-week deployment of an AI code-feedback tool in lower-secondary computing.

_recorded.outcome: Students using the AI feedback tool fixed bugs faster and submitted more working programs than a control class.
_recorded.context: Lower-secondary computing classroom deployment of an AI tool providing real-time feedback on student code over seven weeks.

examples.abstract: An inoculation 'prebunking' game was tested with secondary students to build resistance to misinformation. Players became better at spotting manipulation techniques in headlines, with gains persisting two weeks later. The trial randomised classes to game or control.
examples.statement: Players became better at spotting manipulation techniques in headlines, with gains persisting two weeks later.

gold.outcome: A prebunking game improves detection of misinformation techniques, with gains persisting two weeks.
gold.context: Class-randomised trial of an inoculation game against misinformation in secondary students.

_recorded.outcome: Students improved at identifying misinformation manipulation techniques in headlines, with gains persisting two weeks later.
_recorded.context: A randomised trial of an inoculation 'prebunking' game with secondary school students, randomising classes to game or control.

examples.abstract: This working paper outlines the architecture of a conversational chatbot for language practice. We detail the dialogue-management design and planned classroom integration. No learning outcomes were measured in this phase.
examples.statement: We detail the dialogue-management design and planned classroom integration.

gold.context: Working paper describing the design of a language-practice chatbot.

_recorded.context: Working paper describing the architecture and dialogue-management design of a conversational chatbot for language practice with planned classroom integration.

examples.abstract: A synthesis of classroom formative-assessment studies examined effects on attainment. The evidence indicates that frequent, feedback-rich formative assessment raises achievement across grade levels. Effects were larger when feedback was specific and actionable.
examples.statement: The evidence indicates that frequent, feedback-rich formative assessment raises achievement across grade levels.

gold.outcome: Frequent feedback-rich formative assessment raises achievement across grades.
gold.context: Synthesis of classroom formative-assessment studies across grade levels.

_recorded.outcome: Frequent, feedback-rich formative assessment is associated with higher achievement, with larger effects when feedback is specific and actionable.
_recorded.context: A synthesis of classroom formative-assessment studies examining effects on attainment across grade levels.

examples.abstract: A digital game targeting fraction concepts was trialled with upper-primary pupils. Players developed stronger conceptual understanding of fractions than a worksheet group. The four-week trial involved 110 pupils.
examples.statement: Players developed stronger conceptual understanding of fractions than a worksheet group.

gold.outcome: A fractions game improves conceptual understanding over worksheets.
gold.context: Four-week trial of a digital fractions game with upper-primary pupils.

_recorded.outcome: Pupils using the digital game developed stronger conceptual understanding of fractions than those using worksheets.
_recorded.context: Four-week trial with 110 upper-primary pupils comparing a fraction-focused digital game to worksheet-based instruction.

examples.abstract: Pair programming was introduced in a secondary computing course and compared with solo work. Paired students solved problems more successfully and reported higher confidence. The study ran across two terms with rotating pairs.
examples.statement: Paired students solved problems more successfully and reported higher confidence.

gold.outcome: Pair programming improves problem-solving success and confidence.
gold.context: Two-term comparison of pair programming versus solo work in secondary computing.

_recorded.outcome: Students working in pairs solved problems more successfully and reported higher confidence than those working alone.
_recorded.context: Pair programming intervention introduced in a secondary computing course, compared with solo work over two terms with rotating pairs.

examples.abstract: An augmented-reality anatomy app was compared with a textbook in upper-secondary biology. Students using the app were more engaged, but post-test anatomy knowledge did not differ between conditions. The sample comprised three classes.
examples.statement: Students using the app were more engaged, but post-test anatomy knowledge did not differ between conditions.

gold.outcome: An AR anatomy app raises engagement but not knowledge over a textbook.
gold.context: Classroom comparison of an AR anatomy app versus a textbook in upper-secondary biology.

_recorded.outcome: Students using the augmented-reality app showed greater engagement, but anatomy knowledge on the post-test did not differ from the textbook condition.
_recorded.context: Upper-secondary biology classes comparing an augmented-reality anatomy app with a textbook.

examples.abstract: This policy report reviews how school systems address the ethics of AI use in classrooms. It recommends clearer guidance for teachers and students but reports no measured learning outcomes. The report targets regional education authorities.
examples.statement: It recommends clearer guidance for teachers and students but reports no measured learning outcomes.

gold.context: Policy report reviewing how school systems address AI ethics in classrooms.

_recorded.outcome: No learning outcomes were measured; the report recommends clearer guidance for teachers and students on ethical AI use.
_recorded.context: A policy report reviewing how school systems address the ethics of AI use in classrooms, targeting regional education authorities.

examples.abstract: A review examined mother-tongue-based instruction in the early grades of multilingual countries. The evidence shows that initial literacy in the home language improves early reading outcomes. Transfer to the second language was also supported.
examples.statement: The evidence shows that initial literacy in the home language improves early reading outcomes.

gold.outcome: Mother-tongue-based early instruction improves early reading outcomes.
gold.context: Review of mother-tongue-based instruction in the early grades of multilingual countries.

_recorded.outcome: Initial literacy in the home language is associated with improved early reading outcomes, with support for transfer to a second language.
_recorded.context: A review of mother-tongue-based instruction in the early grades of multilingual countries.

examples.abstract: A randomised study compared worked examples with conventional problem-solving for teaching algebra. Students given worked examples learned more efficiently and scored higher on a delayed test. The trial involved 200 lower-secondary students.
examples.statement: Students given worked examples learned more efficiently and scored higher on a delayed test.

gold.outcome: Worked examples improve learning efficiency and delayed-test performance in algebra.
gold.context: Randomised comparison of worked examples versus problem-solving in lower-secondary algebra.

_recorded.outcome: Students taught with worked examples learned more efficiently and scored higher on a delayed test than those using conventional problem-solving.
_recorded.context: A randomised trial with 200 lower-secondary students comparing worked examples with conventional problem-solving for teaching algebra.

examples.abstract: A virtual-reality perspective-taking experience was tested with secondary students to foster empathy. Immediately afterwards students reported higher empathy, but the effect was not measured beyond the session. The study had no active control.
examples.statement: Immediately afterwards students reported higher empathy, but the effect was not measured beyond the session.

gold.outcome: A VR perspective-taking experience raises immediate self-reported empathy, with durability untested.
gold.context: Uncontrolled test of a VR perspective-taking experience with secondary students.

_recorded.outcome: Students reported higher empathy immediately after the intervention, but no effect was measured beyond the session.
_recorded.context: Secondary school students participated in a virtual-reality perspective-taking intervention aimed at fostering empathy.

examples.abstract: We compared longhand and laptop note-taking among lower-secondary students during science lessons. Students taking longhand notes recalled slightly more conceptual content on a later quiz. Differences were small and varied by topic.
examples.statement: Students taking longhand notes recalled slightly more conceptual content on a later quiz.

gold.outcome: Longhand note-taking yields slightly better conceptual recall than laptop notes.
gold.context: Comparison of longhand versus laptop note-taking in lower-secondary science.

_recorded.outcome: Students who took longhand notes recalled slightly more conceptual content on a later quiz, though differences were small and varied by topic.
_recorded.context: Comparison of longhand versus laptop note-taking among lower-secondary students during science lessons.

examples.abstract: An all-girls coding club ran weekly across a school year in an underserved district. Participants reported higher coding self-efficacy and interest in computing careers. Engagement was measured by surveys and attendance.
examples.statement: Participants reported higher coding self-efficacy and interest in computing careers.

gold.outcome: An all-girls coding club raises coding self-efficacy and interest in computing.
